rot.outpost.ideia.sveshnikov.e1: Attack: a square is weak when none of the opponent's pawns can attack it any more. This happens when the pawns that guarded it have already advanced or been traded.
rot.outpost.ideia.sveshnikov.e2: This is the Sicilian Defence, Sveshnikov Variation. Black traded the c-pawn on d4 and pushed the e-pawn to e5. Look at the d5-square.
rot.outpost.ideia.sveshnikov.l1: The knight goes to d5. No black pawn can attack it: the c-pawn was traded, and the one on e5 has already gone past that square.
rot.outpost.ideia.sveshnikov.l2: That is why d5 is a weak square for Black. The knight on it, supported by the pawn on e4, occupies an outpost: no pawn can drive it away, and from there it reaches into Black's camp.
rot.outpost.ideia.sveshnikov.l3: Black develops the bishop to e7 and prepares to castle.
rot.outpost.ideia.sveshnikov.l4: The bishop captures the knight on f6, which could have captured the one on d5 and broken up the outpost.
rot.outpost.ideia.sveshnikov.l5: The bishop recaptured. Without the knight on f6, Black has one piece fewer to contest d5.
rot.outpost.ideia.sveshnikov.l6: In positions like this one, the outpost is worth something as long as the opponent cannot trade the piece on it. Before taking a piece to an outpost, check who can trade it.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.e1: Attack: an outpost also serves the attack. This position comes from a London System game played on Lichess. The knight on e5 sits on an outpost: Black has no f-pawn, and the d5-pawn has already gone past that square.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.e2: Supported by the pawn on d4, the knight attacks g6 and f7, near the black king on h7. The knight on g4 could trade it, but here White strikes first.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.p: Find the move that makes use of the knight on e5 against the black king.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.certo: The queen captures the pawn on g6 with check. The king cannot recapture, because the knight on e5 defends g6.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.revela: The queen captures the pawn on g6 with check: the knight on e5 defends g6, so the king cannot recapture.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.err.e5f7.1: With this move, Black escapes: the knight captures the rook, but it leaves e5, and g6 loses its defender.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.err.e5f7.2: Back to the position: leave the knight on e5 and look for the move that relies on it.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.err.e5g4.1: With this move, Black escapes: the knight captures the one on g4, but it leaves the outpost, and g6 loses its defender.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.err.e5g4.2: Back to the position: leave the knight on e5 and look for the move that relies on it.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.err.e5g6.1: With this move, Black has a resource: the knight on g4 goes to f2 and attacks the queen on d3.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.err.e5g6.2: Back to the position: the knight defends g6 from e5. Look for a queen move.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.fora: That move does not use the knight on e5. Look for a queen move that relies on it.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.volta: Try again: use the knight on e5.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.l0: The black king is in check, and the queen on g6 still covers the squares around it.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.l1: The king only has h8 to get out of check.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.l2: The knight leaves the outpost and captures the rook on f7 with mate: the queen on g6 covers g7, g8 and h7.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.l3: The knight on e5 defended the queen on g6 and then delivered mate on f7. On an outpost near the enemy king, the knight can decide the attack.
rot.outpost.ideia.london.l4: Notice that the first move was a queen check. With checks and captures available, calculate before thinking about squares.
rot.outpost.demos.regra.1: Attacking demonstration: another London System game from Lichess. The knight on e5 sits on an outpost: Black has no f-pawn, the d5-pawn has gone past that square, and the pawn on d4 supports it. The knight on c6 could trade it, but White moves first.
rot.outpost.demos.regra.2: The knight leaves the outpost and captures the pawn on g6. From there it attacks the queen on e7 and the rook on h8 at the same time.
rot.outpost.demos.regra.3: Black cannot save both queen and rook with a single move, so they capture the knight with the h7-pawn. That opens the h-file.
rot.outpost.demos.regra.4: The rook goes down the h-file and captures the rook on h8. White gave the knight and won a rook and a pawn.
rot.outpost.demos.regra.5: The outpost gave the knight a safe square near Black's kingside. It left it with a double attack, and the material went to White.
rot.outpost.demos.regra2.1: Attacking demonstration: once more a London System game from Lichess. The knight on g5 sits on an outpost: Black has no f-pawn, the h5-pawn has gone past that square, and the pawn on h4 supports it.
rot.outpost.demos.regra2.2: The knight leaves the outpost for e6 with check and now defends g7.
rot.outpost.demos.regra2.3: The black king goes to g8, the only square it has left.
rot.outpost.demos.regra2.4: The queen captures the bishop on g7 with mate, defended by the knight on e6.
rot.outpost.demos.regra2.5: From the g5 outpost, the knight reached e6 and f7, near the black king. With the queen on g6, that was enough for mate.
rot.outpost.demos.excecao.1: Defensive demonstration: now let us think from Black's side. In this London System, White is going to bring the knight to e5. Look at the bishop on d6.
rot.outpost.demos.excecao.2: The knight goes to e5, supported by the pawn on d4, and attacks the knight on c6.
rot.outpost.demos.excecao.3: The bishop on d6 captures the knight, so as not to leave it on e5. In return, Black gives up the bishop.
rot.outpost.demos.excecao.4: The d4-pawn recaptures. There is now a pawn on e5, and the outpost no longer exists.
rot.outpost.demos.excecao.5: The knight on f6, attacked by the e5-pawn, retreats to d7.
rot.outpost.demos.excecao.6: The f7-pawn could still go to f6 against the knight: e5 was not a weak square. And the bishop on d6 could trade it. Check both before bringing the piece.
rot.outpost.pratica.valeAqui.enunciado: Your knight on e7, supported by the pawn on d6, is well placed. Is this a moment to think about squares, or is there something more forcing? Play as White and find the best move.
rot.outpost.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The queen gave check on f7, the black queen blocked on g7, and your queen captured the rook on c4. With checks and captures available, calculate before thinking about squares.
rot.outpost.pratica.valeAqui.err.e7g6: The knight captures the pawn on g6, but the black queen goes to g7 and threatens the knight, and the game becomes level. Look for a forcing move with your queen.
rot.outpost.pratica.valeAqui.err.e7c6: The knight goes to c6, but the black queen gives check on c5 and attacks it. Look for a forcing move with your queen.
rot.outpost.pratica.valeAqui.err.f3d3: The queen goes to d3, but the black queen gives check on d4, and Black keeps a rook against your knight. Look for a forcing move with your queen.
rot.outpost.pratica.valeAqui.err2: After the queen trade, Black has both rooks against your rook and knight, and is better. Look for an undefended black piece.
rot.outpost.pratica.posto.enunciado: Look for a weak square near the black king for your knight on e4, with the support of a pawn. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.outpost.pratica.posto.fim: The knight entered f6, supported by the e5-pawn, with check and attacking the rook on e8 and the bishop on d7. The queen captured the knight, and the e5-pawn captured the queen.
rot.outpost.pratica.posto.err.f3h4: The knight on f3 captures the one on h4, but the d5-pawn captures your knight on e4. Look for a weak square for the knight on e4.
rot.outpost.pratica.posto.err.e3g5: The queen gives check on g5, but the black queen captures it. Look for a weak square for the knight on e4.
rot.outpost.pratica.posto.err.e4g5: On g5 the knight has no pawn support: the bishop goes to h6 and attacks it. Look for a square supported by a pawn.
rot.outpost.pratica.postoPreto.enunciado: Now let us think from Black's side. The white king has stayed in the centre. Look for a weak square near it for your knight on e5. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.outpost.pratica.postoPreto.fim: The knight entered f3 with check, supported by the g4-pawn: no white pawn can reach it. The king went to e2, and the queen gave mate on d2, defended by the knight, or on d3, defended by the c4-pawn.
rot.outpost.pratica.postoPreto.err.e5f7: The knight captures the queen, but your king on a5 is left without defence: the bishop captures the c4-pawn and opens the way for White's attack. Look for a check.
rot.outpost.pratica.postoPreto.err.a8d8: The rook goes to d8, but threatens nothing, and the knight on c7 goes to d5, near your king. Look for a weak square near the white king.
rot.outpost.pratica.postoPreto.err.e5d3: On d3 the knight gives check, but the bishop on f1 captures it, and your king stays exposed. Look for another square for the knight.
